facts.text: The Royal Hawaiian Resort opened in 1927, offering guests nearly a century of history displayed in a 520‑square‑foot exhibition.
The six‑story, 400‑room structure was built in Spanish‑Moorish style, a design popular in the era and inspired by Rudolph Valentino.
In 1969 the resort expanded with the Mailani Tower, adding a modern oceanfront experience to its historic charm.
The Royal Hawaiian Resort is nicknamed the “Pink Palace of the Pacific,” a title that reflects its distinctive color and heritage.
Guests can join weekly historical tours inside the resort’s arcade near the front desk, where rare archival materials trace the hotel’s evolution.
The resort’s historic wing and Mailani Tower showcase contrasting architectural styles, offering a visual narrative of Waikiki’s development over time.
